resources.string: Reads notifications from apps you choose

Mika\'s phone helper will turn on \"Notification access\" for Mika in system settings.\n\nThis is a sensitive permission: technically it allows reading all notifications. Mika only reads the apps you tick on this page. You can revoke it any time in system settings.
Phone control isn\'t set up yet. Set it up first, or use \"Grant access\" above.
Couldn\'t grant it this way. Try \"Grant access\" above.

Turning the switch off: nothing more is read or sent, and unhandled notifications and stored notification text are deleted. Topics, contacts and digests already gathered stay; delete them under “What Mika has gathered”. Notification access itself stays granted until you revoke it in system settings.
No model is set up. Choose one in Settings › Models first.
The provider or model changed. Paused until you confirm again.
Today\'s triage token share is used up. Triage resumes tomorrow.
Today\'s triage request share is used up. Triage resumes tomorrow.
Waiting for the running task to finish
Can\'t reach the model; will try again later.
Proactive model calls stop for the day at this limit, or after %1$d requests. Triage stops at %2$d%% of each, leaving the rest for other proactive features.
new content, will check again later
this app reached today\'s alert limit
I picked out %1$d notifications you may want to look at:
%1$d more are not listed; open the reminder again to see them.
Tell me which one you want me to handle. Just reply here.
Not yet confirmed which model the notifications go to

App access settings can\'t be read, so proactive features are on hold: no notifications are read and nothing is sent to the model. What\'s already saved is kept. Reset them on the App access page to resume.
The list of apps to read could not be loaded, so nothing is being read. Choose the apps again; what was gathered before is not affected.
That change could not be saved (storage may be full). Please choose it again. If you chose “Not read”, the app is already no longer being read.

Each app can be: not read, Low (sorted and flagged only), Medium (also gathered from), or High (what is gathered may go into tasks). At Bold, what is gathered from Medium apps goes into tasks too. Chat apps carry other people\'s words, so think before letting one into tasks.

Sent to the model: the title, text and recent messages of notifications from the apps you chose, one app at a time, to the model you confirmed; plus the app\'s package name, whether it is a group or private chat, whether you opened or dismissed each notification, and the names of up to 30 existing topics. Daily, weekly and monthly digests are made only from sentences already written, not from the notification text. The daily one is also given the names of the chats.

Stored on this phone, encrypted: short topics, and the names and guessed relationships of the people and groups you chat with. Sorting results stay in memory only. When you open a reminder, those notifications are written into a conversation and kept like your other conversations; if you continue there, that text goes to the model doing the work. Turning this off, or deleting or clearing things under “What Mika has gathered”, does not delete that conversation.
Daily digest is on, so these are also stored: notification text (up to 2 days), the notes made from it (8 days), each day\'s digest (35 days), weekly digests (26 weeks) and monthly digests (2 years).
Apart from reminders you open, notification text is not stored: it stays in memory only until it has been handled.
Its notifications are not read. Its stored notification text and the digest lines made from it are deleted; topics and contacts stay.

The text of notifications from the apps you chose (title, text and recent messages) will be sent to %1$s, model %2$s, to decide which are worth flagging and to gather short topics and the names and guessed relationships of the people and groups you chat with. What is gathered is stored on this phone, encrypted.\n\nIf the provider or model changes later, this pauses until you confirm again. Turning the main switch off stops all sending.
